source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 12 (PDF 258-282, printed 255-279); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 12 (Human Skeletal and Muscular Systems), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The internal framework of the body called skeleton is made of:

options.text: bones, cartilage and other connective tissues

blocks.explanation: Bones, cartilage and other connective tissues make the skeleton, which supports the body, protects vital organs and produces movement (12.1).

book_ref.quote: make an internal framework called skeleton that provides structural support

blocks.prompt: 2 The tough membrane covering the surface of a bone is called:
blocks.explanation: The bone's surface is covered by a tough membrane called periosteum; perichondrium covers cartilage (12.1).

book_ref.quote: covered by a tough membrane called periosteum

blocks.prompt: 3 The thick, hard layer under the periosteum that makes up the majority of the bone tissue is:
blocks.explanation: The thick layer under the periosteum is compact bone; it makes up most of the bone tissue (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It makes up the majority of the bone tissue

blocks.prompt: 4 The basic structural units of compact bone are:
blocks.explanation: Compact bone is built of Haversian systems, each made of lamellae, lacunae with osteocytes and a Haversian canal (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The basic structural units of compact bone are called Haversian systems

blocks.prompt: 5 The needle-shaped crystals in the lamellae of bone are made of:
blocks.explanation: Lamellae are mineralized matrix with collagen fibres and needle-shaped crystals of calcium phosphate (12.1).

book_ref.quote: small, needle-shaped crystals of calcium phosphate

blocks.prompt: 6 Bone is both strong and flexible because:

options.text: its calcium phosphate crystals are rigid while its collagen is flexible
its collagen is rigid while its crystals are flexible
it has no minerals in its matrix
it is covered by synovial fluid

blocks.explanation: The crystals are brittle but rigid, giving strength; collagen is flexible but weak; together bone is strong and flexible (12.1).

book_ref.quote: As a result, bone is both strong and flexible.

blocks.prompt: 7 In a Haversian system, the small spaces between lamellae in which osteocytes lie are called:
blocks.explanation: The lamellae are separated by small spaces called lacunae, in which the mature bone cells (osteocytes) lie (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Osteocytes, which are mature bone cells, are located in the lacunae.

blocks.prompt: 8 Osteocytes are connected to each other and to the Haversian canal by small channels called:
blocks.explanation: Small channels called canaliculi connect osteocytes to each other and to the Haversian canal (12.1).

book_ref.quote: by small channels called canaliculi

blocks.prompt: 9 The central Haversian canal of a Haversian system contains:

options.text: blood vessels, nerves and lymphatic vessels

blocks.explanation: The Haversian canal, surrounded by lamellae, contains blood vessels, nerves and lymphatic vessels (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatic vessels.

blocks.prompt: 10 The small channels that run perpendicular to the Haversian canals connect them with each other and with the:
blocks.explanation: Perpendicular channels connect the Haversian canals with each other and with the periosteum; they also carry blood vessels, nerves and lymphatic vessels (12.1).

book_ref.quote: run perpendicular to the Haversian canals

blocks.prompt: 11 Spongy bone is light and strong because it has:
blocks.explanation: Spongy bone lies beneath compact bone and has a latticework of bony spikes that make it light and strong (12.1).

book_ref.quote: latticework structure consisting of bony spikes

blocks.prompt: 12 The broad ends of a long bone are called:
blocks.explanation: The broad ends are the epiphysis; the middle part along the length is the diaphysis or shaft (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The broad ends of a bone are called epiphysis

blocks.prompt: 13 Red bone marrow produces:

options.text: red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells

blocks.explanation: Red bone marrow, found in spongy bone, ends of long bones, ribs, vertebrae, sternum and pelvis, produces red cells, platelets and white cells (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It produces red blood cells, platelets, and white blood cells.

blocks.prompt: 14 Yellow bone marrow fills the shafts of long bones and consists mostly of:
blocks.explanation: Yellow marrow is mostly fat cells and is an energy reserve; after severe blood loss it can turn into red marrow (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It consists mostly of fat cells and serves as an energy reserve.

blocks.prompt: 15 Despite their number and size, bones make up:

options.text: more than 50% of the body's mass
less than 20% of the body's mass

blocks.explanation: Bones make up less than 20% of the body's mass; they are moist, living tissues, not dry rigid structures (12.1).

book_ref.quote: bones make up less than 20% of the body

blocks.prompt: 16 Bone-forming cells that synthesize and secrete unmineralized ground substance are:
blocks.explanation: Osteoblasts form bone by secreting unmineralized ground substance; when surrounded by matrix they become osteocytes (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Osteoblasts are bone forming cells that synthesize

blocks.prompt: 17 Osteoclasts develop from:
blocks.explanation: Osteoclasts develop from macrophages and carry out bone resorption (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Osteoclasts develop from macrophages

blocks.prompt: 18 During bone resorption, osteoclasts break down bone and release into the blood:
blocks.explanation: Osteoclasts break down bone and release calcium and phosphate into blood; this is important for growth and repair of bone (12.1).

book_ref.quote: they break down bone and release calcium and phosphate in blood

blocks.prompt: 19 The process of bone formation is called:
blocks.explanation: Bone formation is osteogenesis; it begins in the embryo and continues throughout life (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The process of bone formation is also called osteogenesis.

blocks.prompt: 20 The step by which cartilage is replaced by bone by the deposition of minerals is called:
blocks.explanation: Replacement of cartilage by bone through deposition of minerals is ossification (12.1, Fig. 12.3).

book_ref.quote: The step by which cartilage is replaced by bone by the deposition of minerals is called ossification

blocks.prompt: 21 In the formation of a long bone, when the centre of the cartilage calcifies, the chondrocytes there:
blocks.explanation: The chondrocytes in the calcified centre die and leave cavities; blood vessels enter these cavities and bring osteoblasts and osteoclasts (12.1).

book_ref.quote: the chondrocytes (cartilage cells) in this area die, leaving behind cavities

blocks.prompt: 22 When a long bone is fully formed from cartilage, some cartilage remains only at the:
blocks.explanation: All cartilage changes to bone except some at the articular (joint) surfaces of the bones (12.1).

book_ref.quote: remains only at the articular (joint) surfaces of the bones

blocks.prompt: 23 Which bones develop directly into hard bone without forming cartilage first?
blocks.explanation: A few bones, e.g. some skull bones, develop directly into bone; long bones such as femur and humerus form from cartilage (12.1).

book_ref.quote: some bones of the skull, develop directly into hard bone

blocks.prompt: 24 Bone remodelling after the bones are fully formed involves:

options.text: breakdown of old bone by osteoblasts only
conversion of yellow marrow into bone
breakdown of old bone by osteoclasts and formation of new bone by osteoblasts

blocks.explanation: Remodelling is ongoing osteogenesis: osteoclasts break down old bone and osteoblasts form new bone (12.1).

book_ref.quote: osteogenesis continues in the form of bone remodelling

blocks.prompt: 25 The layer of connective tissue that surrounds cartilage is:
blocks.explanation: Perichondrium surrounds cartilage and contains blood vessels, lymphatic vessels and nerves that supply it (12.1).

book_ref.quote: A layer of connective tissue called perichondrium surrounds the cartilage.

blocks.prompt: 26 Cartilage heals very slowly because:

options.text: its matrix has no blood vessels and its cells are supplied by diffusion
its matrix contains calcium phosphate crystals

blocks.explanation: There are no blood vessels inside the cartilage matrix; the cells get supplies by diffusion, so it heals very slowly (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The cells of cartilage are supplied by diffusion.

blocks.prompt: 27 Chondrocytes are:

options.text: cartilage cells that synthesize and maintain the cartilage matrix

blocks.explanation: Chondrocytes are cartilage cells lying in lacunae; they synthesize and maintain the cartilage matrix (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The cartilage cells, called chondrocytes, are present within small spaces called lacunae

blocks.prompt: 28 The most common type of cartilage, found in the nose, trachea and articulating surfaces of bones, is:
blocks.explanation: Hyaline cartilage is the most common type: nose, trachea and articulating surfaces of bones in joints (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Hyaline cartilage is the most common type

blocks.prompt: 29 Fibrocartilage is found in:

options.text: intervertebral discs and the pubic symphysis

blocks.explanation: Fibrocartilage is found where there is high stress and tension, such as intervertebral discs and the pubic symphysis (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Fibrocartilage is found in areas of the body that experience high stress

blocks.prompt: 30 The cartilage of the external ear and epiglottis is:
blocks.explanation: Elastic cartilage is found in the external ear and epiglottis (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Elastic cartilage is found in the external ear and epiglottis.

blocks.prompt: 31 The cartilage matrix that gives strength, flexibility and resistance to compression is composed of:

options.text: collagen, elastin, proteoglycans and other fibres

blocks.explanation: The cartilage matrix is composed of collagen, elastin, proteoglycans and other fibres (12.1).

book_ref.quote: composed of collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, and other fibres

blocks.prompt: 32 The human skeletal system consists of:
blocks.explanation: The human skeletal system has 206 bones, in axial and appendicular divisions (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Human skeletal system consists of 206 bones.

blocks.prompt: 33 The human skull consists of:
blocks.explanation: The skull has 22 bones: 8 cranial bones and 14 facial bones (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It consists of the following 22 bones

blocks.prompt: 34 Which of these is an unpaired bone of the cranium?
blocks.explanation: Unpaired cranial bones: frontal, occipital, ethmoid, sphenoid; parietal and temporal are paired; zygomatic is a facial bone (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The 4 unpaired bones are frontal bone, occipital bone

blocks.prompt: 35 The two unpaired facial bones are:
blocks.explanation: Of the 14 facial bones, mandible (jaw bone) and vomer are unpaired; the other 6 kinds are paired (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The 2 unpaired bones are mandible (jaw bone) and vomer.

blocks.prompt: 36 The middle ear ossicles are:
blocks.explanation: The middle ears have 6 bones (3 pairs), the ossicles: malleus, incus and stapes (12.1).

book_ref.quote: These are called ossicles and include malleus, incus and stapes.

blocks.prompt: 37 The small single bone at the base of the skull below the tongue that does not articulate with any other bone of the head is:
blocks.explanation: The hyoid is the neck bone at the base of the skull below the tongue; it does not articulate with any other bone of the head (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It does not articulate with any other bone of head.

blocks.prompt: 38 The first cervical vertebra is called:
blocks.explanation: Of the seven cervical (neck) vertebrae, the first is the atlas and the second is the axis (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The first one is called atlas and the second one is called axis.

blocks.prompt: 39 The rib-carrying vertebrae of the chest region are the:
blocks.explanation: The twelve thoracic vertebrae carry the ribs and are found in the chest region (12.1).

book_ref.quote: These are rib-carrying vertebrae and are found in chest region.

blocks.prompt: 40 The sacrum is formed by the fusion of:
blocks.explanation: Five fused sacral vertebrae form the sacrum, which articulates with the iliac bones to form the back of the pelvis (12.1).

book_ref.quote: These are five fused vertebrae forming the sacrum.

blocks.prompt: 41 Sacral and coccygeal vertebrae are together called:
blocks.explanation: Sacral and coccygeal vertebrae are together called pelvic vertebrae (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Sacral and coccygeal vertebrae are together called pelvic vertebrae.

blocks.prompt: 42 The 11th and 12th pairs of ribs are called floating ribs because they:

options.text: do not attach to the sternum
attach to the sternum by separate costal cartilages
attach to the sternum by a common costal cartilage
do not attach to the vertebrae

blocks.explanation: The last 2 pairs (11th and 12th) do not attach to the sternum, so they are floating ribs (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The last 2 pairs of ribs (11th and 12th) are known as floating ribs

blocks.prompt: 43 True ribs attach to the sternum:

options.text: they do not attach to the sternum

blocks.explanation: The first 7 pairs attach directly to the sternum by separate costal cartilages (true ribs); 8th-10th share a common costal cartilage (12.1).

book_ref.quote: attach directly with the sternum by means of separate costal cartilages

blocks.prompt: 44 The pectoral girdle consists of:

options.text: a pair of clavicles and a pair of scapulae
a pair of humeri and the sternum

blocks.explanation: The pectoral girdle has 2 pairs: clavicles (collar bones) and scapulae (shoulder bones) (12.1).

book_ref.quote: a pair of clavicles (collar bones) and a pair of scapulae

blocks.prompt: 45 The spherical head of the humerus fits into the:
blocks.explanation: The humerus head fits into the glenoid cavity; the femur head fits into the acetabulum (12.1).

book_ref.quote: which fits into the glenoid cavity

blocks.prompt: 46 The forearm bone on the outer (thumb) side is the:
blocks.explanation: Ulna is on the inner side and radius on the outer (thumb) side; ulna is slightly bigger (12.1).

book_ref.quote: radius is on outer side (thumb side)

blocks.prompt: 47 The eight short bones of the wrist, in two rows, are the:
blocks.explanation: The wrist has eight carpals in two rows (the book's 'carpels' is a misprint; carpels are parts of a flower) (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The eight wrist bones are the carpals

blocks.prompt: 48 The bones that make up the palm of the hand are the:
blocks.explanation: Five metacarpals make up the palm of the hand (12.1).

book_ref.quote: These bones make up the palm of the hand.

blocks.prompt: 49 Each forelimb (arm, wrist, hand, fingers) consists of:
blocks.explanation: Each forelimb has 30 bones: humerus 1, ulna and radius 2, carpals 8, metacarpals 5, phalanges 14 (12.1).

book_ref.quote: consists of the following 30 bones

blocks.prompt: 50 Each hip bone of the pelvic girdle contains three bones:
blocks.explanation: Each hip bone contains the ilium, ischium and pubis (the book prints 'ileum'; the ileum is part of the small intestine) (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The hip bone is made of the ilium, ischium and pubis

blocks.prompt: 51 The bony socket in each hip bone, formed by the fusion of three bones, is the:
blocks.explanation: Each hip bone has a bony socket, the acetabulum, into which the head of the femur fits (12.1).

book_ref.quote: there is a bony socket, called acetabulum

blocks.prompt: 52 The two hip bones are joined at the front by the:
blocks.explanation: At the front the hip bones are joined by the pubic symphysis, a cartilaginous joint connecting the pubic bones at the midline (12.1).

book_ref.quote: The two hip bones are joined at the front by the pubic symphysis

blocks.prompt: 53 The patella (kneecap) is embedded in:

options.text: a long tendon running over the knee joint

blocks.explanation: The patella is embedded in a long tendon that runs over the knee joint (12.1).

book_ref.quote: It is embedded in a long tendon which runs over the knee joint.

blocks.prompt: 54 The shin bone, the large bone of the leg, is the:
blocks.explanation: Tibia (shin bone) is the large bone of the leg; fibula is the thin outer bone (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Tibia or shin bone is the large bone in the leg.

blocks.prompt: 55 The ankle is formed by:
blocks.explanation: Seven tarsals, short bones tightly attached together, form the ankle (12.1).

book_ref.quote: These are short bones which are tightly attached to form the ankle.

blocks.prompt: 56 The big toe has:
blocks.explanation: Each toe has 3 phalanges but the big toe has 2, giving 14 phalanges in a foot (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Each toe has 3 phalanges while the big toe comprises 2 phalanges.

blocks.prompt: 57 A joint is a place where:

options.text: two bones or bone and cartilage come together

blocks.explanation: A joint is where two bones, or bone and cartilage, come together (12.1).

book_ref.quote: A joint is a place where two bones or bone and cartilage come together.

blocks.prompt: 58 In fibrous joints the bones are connected by fibrous connective tissue consisting mainly of:
blocks.explanation: Fibrous joints are joined directly by fibrous connective tissue, mainly collagen, and permit no movement (12.1).

book_ref.quote: by fibrous connective tissue consisting mainly of collagen

blocks.prompt: 59 Sutures are fibrous joints found only between the:
blocks.explanation: Sutures occur only between the immovable bones of the skull (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Sutures that occur only between the immovable bones of the skull.

blocks.prompt: 60 The joint between the first rib and the sternum is a cartilaginous joint in which the bones are connected by:
blocks.explanation: In some cartilaginous joints, e.g. first rib and sternum, the bones are joined by hyaline cartilage; pubic symphysis uses fibrocartilage (12.1).

book_ref.quote: For example, the joint between the first rib and sternum.

blocks.prompt: 61 In a synovial joint, the ends of the bones are covered by articular cartilage, which is:
blocks.explanation: Articular cartilage is smooth, tough, elastic hyaline cartilage that gives a frictionless surface for movement (12.1).

book_ref.quote: called articular cartilage, covers the ends of the bones in the joint

blocks.prompt: 62 Synovial fluid that lubricates a synovial joint is secreted by the:
blocks.explanation: The fibrous capsule has outer ligaments and an inner synovial membrane, which secretes synovial fluid (12.1).

book_ref.quote: inner lining of synovial membrane, which secretes synovial fluid

blocks.prompt: 63 Based on the range of motion, synovial joints are of:
blocks.explanation: There are six main types of synovial joints: ball-and-socket, hinge, pivot, ellipsoidal, saddle and gliding (12.1).

book_ref.quote: There are six main types of synovial joints based on the range of motion.

blocks.prompt: 64 A joint that allows motion in all directions, as in the shoulder and hip, is a:
blocks.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints allow motion in all directions, e.g. shoulder and hip joints (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Ball-and-socket joints allow motion in all directions

blocks.prompt: 65 The joint between the first and second vertebrae of the neck is a:
blocks.explanation: Pivot joints allow rotation around a single axis, e.g. between the first and second neck vertebrae (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Pivot joints allow rotational movement around a single axis

blocks.prompt: 66 The thumb joint, where one bone has a concave and the other a convex surface, is a:
blocks.explanation: Saddle joints allow movement in two planes because one surface is concave and the other convex, e.g. thumb joint (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Saddle joints allow movement in two planes because one bone has a concave surface

blocks.prompt: 67 The joint of the wrist with the radius, which allows movement in two planes but no rotation, is:
blocks.explanation: Ellipsoidal joints allow movement in two planes but not rotation, e.g. joint of wrist with radius (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Ellipsoidal joints allow movement in two planes, but not rotation

blocks.prompt: 68 Elbow and knee joints are hinge joints because they allow movement:

options.text: around a single axis by rotation

blocks.explanation: Hinge joints, like a door hinge, allow movement in only one plane, e.g. elbow and knee (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Hinge joints allow movement in only one plane, like a door hinge

blocks.prompt: 69 In total joint replacement, the damaged joint is replaced with:

options.text: a healthy joint from a donor
an artificial joint made of metal, plastic or ceramic
only an artificial part of the joint

blocks.explanation: Total joint replacement replaces the entire damaged joint with an artificial one of metal, plastic or ceramic; a donor joint is allograft transplantation (12.1).

book_ref.quote: the entire damaged joint is replaced with an artificial joint made of metal, plastic, or ceramic

blocks.prompt: 70 The human vertebral column distributes weight evenly and maintains balance during standing and walking because it has:
blocks.explanation: The S-shaped curve of the human vertebral column distributes weight evenly and keeps balance in bipedal posture (12.1).

book_ref.quote: distinctive S-shaped curve

blocks.prompt: 71 The structure of the human foot that absorbs shock and distributes weight evenly is its:

options.text: seven tarsals fused into one bone

blocks.explanation: The longitudinal arch of the human foot absorbs shock and distributes weight evenly across the foot (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Human foot has a longitudinal arch that helps to absorb shock

blocks.prompt: 72 When overused and underused muscles due to poor posture pull bones and joints out of alignment, the problem is called:
blocks.explanation: Improper posture causes vertebral misalignment, joint strain and muscle imbalances; the last pulls bones and joints out of alignment (12.1).

book_ref.quote: Overused and underused muscles from poor posture can pull bones

blocks.prompt: 73 A slipped (herniated) disc occurs when:

options.text: uric acid crystals form in the disc
the outer layer of an intervertebral disc tears and its inner gel-like substance leaks out

blocks.explanation: In disc slip the outer layer of the disc tears or ruptures and the inner gel-like substance leaks out and presses on nerves or the spinal cord (12.2).

book_ref.quote: occurs when the outer layer of the intervertebral disc tears or ruptures

blocks.prompt: 74 In severe cases of slipped disc, a symptom may be:
blocks.explanation: Disc slip causes pain, numbness, tingling, muscle weakness and, in severe cases, bowel or bladder dysfunction (12.2).

book_ref.quote: in severe cases, bowel or bladder dysfunction

blocks.prompt: 75 Spondylosis means:

options.text: degeneration of vertebrae, intervertebral discs, ligaments or cartilage of the vertebral column
build-up of uric acid in joints
injury to the ligaments of the ankle

blocks.explanation: Spondylosis is degeneration of vertebrae, discs, ligaments or cartilage of the vertebral column (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Spondylosis means degeneration of vertebrae

blocks.prompt: 76 Spondylosis is most common in the:
blocks.explanation: Spondylosis is most common in the lower back (lumbar vertebrae) and neck (cervical vertebrae) (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Spondylosis is most common in the lower back

blocks.prompt: 77 Sciatica is most often caused by:

options.text: a herniated or bulging disc pressing on the sciatic nerve

blocks.explanation: Sciatica is compression or irritation of the sciatic nerve, often by a herniated or bulging disc; trauma, infection, inflammation and spondylosis also cause it (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Sciatica is often caused by a herniated disc or bulging disc

blocks.prompt: 78 The sciatic nerve runs:

options.text: from the neck into each arm
from the lower back through the buttocks into each leg
from the skull into the jaw
from the chest into the abdomen

blocks.explanation: The sciatic nerve starts from the lower back and goes through the buttocks into each leg (12.2).

book_ref.quote: The sciatic nerve starts from lower back

blocks.prompt: 79 The most common type of arthritis is:
blocks.explanation: Osteoarthritis is the most common type; the articular cartilage softens and disintegrates (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Osteoarthritis is the most common type.

blocks.prompt: 80 Rheumatoid arthritis results from:

options.text: softening of articular cartilage with age
an autoimmune disorder in which the synovial membrane becomes inflamed

blocks.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disorder with inflamed synovial membrane; wrist and hands are most often involved (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Rheumatoid arthritis is the result of an autoimmune disorder

blocks.prompt: 81 In gout, the joint most commonly affected is the joint of the:
blocks.explanation: Gout is caused by uric acid build-up forming crystals in joints; the big toe joint is most commonly affected (12.2).

book_ref.quote: The most common joint affected is the joint of the big toe.

blocks.prompt: 82 In women after menopause, bone loss is accelerated by:
blocks.explanation: After menopause a drop in oestrogen accelerates bone loss, a cause of osteoporosis (12.2).

book_ref.quote: In women, a drop in oestrogen levels after menopause

blocks.prompt: 83 In relation to bone health, vitamin D:

options.text: causes bone loss when taken in the diet

blocks.explanation: Calcium is crucial for bone strength while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; lack of both impairs bone health (12.2).

book_ref.quote: while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium

blocks.prompt: 84 Which treatment is named as a cause of bone loss leading to osteoporosis?
blocks.explanation: Certain treatments such as long-term use of corticosteroids contribute to bone loss (12.2).

book_ref.quote: long-term use of corticosteroids

blocks.prompt: 85 A dislocation is an injury in which:

options.text: the bones in a joint are forced out of their normal positions
the ligaments are stretched but bones stay in place
uric acid crystals form in a joint

blocks.explanation: In a dislocation the bones of a joint are forced out of their normal positions, e.g. by sudden impact or trauma (12.2).

book_ref.quote: A dislocation is when the bones in a joint are forced out of their normal positions.

blocks.prompt: 86 A sprain is an injury to the:

options.text: tendons that attach muscles to bones
ligaments that connect bones in a joint

blocks.explanation: A sprain injures the ligaments of a joint, commonly in the ankle, knee and wrist, when they stretch or tear (12.2).

book_ref.quote: A sprain is an injury to the ligaments that connect bones in a joint.

blocks.prompt: 87 A dislocated joint should be put back in place (reduced) by:
blocks.explanation: Book correction: reduction is done by a doctor, usually with pain relief or anaesthesia and often after an X-ray; physiotherapy helps recovery afterwards (12.2).

book_ref.quote: A dislocated joint is put back in place (reduced) by a doctor

blocks.prompt: 88 After a dislocation, surgery may be needed to:

options.text: repair or tighten the stretched ligaments

blocks.explanation: Surgery may be needed to repair or tighten ligaments stretched by the dislocation (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Surgery may be needed to repair or tighten the stretched ligaments.

blocks.prompt: 89 In first aid for a dislocation, the affected area should be:

options.text: massaged and pulled to re-align the joint
immobilized with a sling or splint, without trying to re-align the joint

blocks.explanation: First aid: immobilize the area with a sling or splint and do not try to re-align the joint (12.2).

book_ref.quote: do not attempt to re-align the dislocated joint

blocks.prompt: 90 An ice pack or cold compress is applied to a sprain or dislocation to:
blocks.explanation: Ice or a cold compress reduces swelling and pain (12.2).

book_ref.quote: Apply an ice pack or cold compress

blocks.prompt: 91 For a dislocation or sprain, the emergency medical service number named in the chapter is:
blocks.explanation: Dislocations and sprains need medical attention: call emergency medical services 1122 or take the person to hospital (12.2).

book_ref.quote: call for emergency medical services 1122

blocks.prompt: 92 Besides moving the body, the contraction and relaxation of muscles:

options.text: provides the force that pushes substances such as blood and food through the body

blocks.explanation: Muscles' contraction and relaxation also provide the force that pushes blood and food through the body (12.3).

book_ref.quote: provides the force that pushes substances, such as blood and food

blocks.prompt: 93 Skeletal muscles are called voluntary muscles because:

options.text: they are found only in the heart
they move substances through hollow organs
their contractions are usually consciously controlled

blocks.explanation: Skeletal muscle contractions are usually consciously controlled, so they are voluntary muscles (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Because their contractions are usually consciously controlled

blocks.prompt: 94 Smooth muscle fibres are:

options.text: spindle-shaped, with a single nucleus and no striations

blocks.explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are spindle-shaped, uninucleate and lack striations (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Smooth muscle fibres are spindle-shaped, have a single nucleus and lack striations.

blocks.prompt: 95 Smooth muscles are present in the walls of:

options.text: the stomach, intestines and blood vessels

blocks.explanation: Smooth muscles occur in the walls of the stomach, intestines, blood vessels and other internal organs; they are involuntary (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Smooth muscles are present in the walls of the stomach, intestines, blood vessels

blocks.prompt: 96 Muscle fibres that branch extensively and are found only in the walls of the heart are:
blocks.explanation: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart wall; its fibres branch extensively (12.3).

book_ref.quote: These are found only in the walls of the heart.

blocks.prompt: 97 A cardiac muscle cell is striated like skeletal muscle but usually has:

options.text: one nucleus located near the centre

blocks.explanation: Cardiac muscle fibres are striated, but each cell usually has one nucleus near the centre (12.3).

book_ref.quote: but each cell usually contains one nucleus located near the centre

blocks.prompt: 98 At the ends of a skeletal muscle, the collagen and connective tissue form:
blocks.explanation: Muscle fibre bundles are enclosed by collagen and connective tissue, which at the muscle's ends form tendons attaching it to bones (12.3).

book_ref.quote: the collagen and connective tissue forms tendons

blocks.prompt: 99 The plasma membrane enclosing a skeletal muscle fibre is called:
blocks.explanation: Each muscle fibre is enclosed by the sarcolemma; its cytoplasm is the sarcoplasm (12.3).

book_ref.quote: enclosed by a plasma membrane called sarcolemma

blocks.prompt: 100 The transverse tubules (T-tubules) of a muscle fibre are formed by:

options.text: the sarcolemma penetrating deep into the cell

blocks.explanation: The sarcolemma penetrates deep into the cell to form hollow tubes, the T-tubules, which reach the ends of the SR (12.3).

book_ref.quote: The sarcolemma penetrates deep into the cell to form hollow elongated tubes

blocks.prompt: 101 In a myofibril, the dark A-bands are created by:
blocks.explanation: Thick myosin filaments create the dark A-bands and thin actin filaments the light I-bands, giving the striated look (12.3).

book_ref.quote: The thick filaments create dark bands called A-bands

blocks.prompt: 102 The smallest unit of muscle contraction is the:
blocks.explanation: The section between two Z-lines is a sarcomere, the smallest unit of muscle contraction (12.3).

book_ref.quote: the smallest unit of muscle contraction

blocks.prompt: 103 The dark line at the centre of the H-band that helps stabilize the thick filaments is the:
blocks.explanation: The centre of the H-band may have a dark M line, which helps stabilize the thick filaments (12.3).

book_ref.quote: a dark line called the M line which helps stabilize the thick filaments

blocks.prompt: 104 The diameter of a thick myofilament is about:
blocks.explanation: Thick myofilaments are about 16 nm across; thin ones are 7-8 nm (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Thick myofilaments, about 16 nm in diameter

blocks.prompt: 105 The diameter of a thin myofilament is:
blocks.explanation: Thin myofilaments are 7-8 nm in diameter, about half the 16 nm of thick myofilaments (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Thin myofilaments, 7-8 nm in diameter

blocks.prompt: 106 Each myosin protein of a thick filament consists of:

options.text: one straight chain with no head
two intertwined polypeptide chains ending in a globular head

blocks.explanation: Each myosin protein has two intertwined polypeptide chains ending in a globular head, which connects to actin during contraction (12.3).

book_ref.quote: two intertwined polypeptide chains, ending in a globular

blocks.prompt: 107 In a relaxed muscle fibre, the myosin binding sites on actin are blocked by:
blocks.explanation: Two tropomyosin strands wrap the actin core, stiffen it and, in a relaxed fibre, block the myosin binding sites (12.3).

book_ref.quote: In a relaxed muscle fibre, they block myosin binding sites on actin.

blocks.prompt: 108 The troponin of thin myofilaments is made of:
blocks.explanation: Troponin has three polypeptides: one inhibitory binding actin, one binding tropomyosin, one binding calcium ions (12.3).

book_ref.quote: It is made of three polypeptides.

blocks.prompt: 109 In a relaxed sarcomere, the myosin heads:

options.text: are bound to actin forming cross-bridges
have hydrolysed ATP into ADP and Pi and are not bound to actin

blocks.explanation: In the relaxed state myosin heads have hydrolysed ATP into ADP and Pi but are not bound to actin, whose sites are blocked by tropomyosin (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Myosin heads have hydrolysed ATP into ADP and Pi.

blocks.prompt: 110 The neurotransmitter released by the motor neuron at the synapse with a muscle fibre is:
blocks.explanation: When a nerve impulse arrives, the motor neuron releases acetylcholine, which stimulates the sarcolemma to produce its own impulses (12.3).

book_ref.quote: a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) is released by motor neuron

blocks.prompt: 111 The calcium ions released into the cytosol during contraction bind to:
blocks.explanation: Calcium ions bind to troponin, which shifts tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin (12.3).

book_ref.quote: These calcium ions bind to troponin

blocks.prompt: 112 The bending of myosin heads towards the centre of the sarcomere, pulling the actin filaments, is called:
blocks.explanation: After forming cross-bridges, myosin heads bend towards the sarcomere centre pulling actin: this is the power stroke (12.3).

book_ref.quote: This pulling action is called a power stroke.

blocks.prompt: 113 Once cross-bridges are formed, the myosin heads:

options.text: take up a new ATP and detach
release ADP and Pi and change their conformation

blocks.explanation: After cross-bridge formation the heads release ADP and Pi and undergo a conformational change (bend) (12.3).

book_ref.quote: the myosin heads release the ADP and Pi

blocks.prompt: 114 A myosin head detaches from actin after the power stroke when it:

options.text: receives a new molecule of ATP

blocks.explanation: A new ATP lets the head detach; splitting it into ADP and Pi resets the head for the next cycle (12.3).

book_ref.quote: the myosin head receives a new molecule of ATP

blocks.prompt: 115 Rigor mortis occurs because after death:

options.text: cells cannot produce ATP, so cross-bridges cannot be broken

blocks.explanation: After death no ATP is produced, so cross-bridges cannot break and muscles stiffen (rigor mortis) (12.3).

book_ref.quote: It causes the muscle stiffness of death, or rigor mortis.

blocks.prompt: 116 The end of a muscle attached to the bone that stays stationary during contraction is the:
blocks.explanation: The end on the stationary bone is the origin; the end on the moving bone is the insertion (12.3).

book_ref.quote: The end attached to the stationary bone during contraction is called the origin

blocks.prompt: 117 The middle part of a skeletal muscle is called the:
blocks.explanation: A muscle has an origin, an insertion and the middle part, the belly (12.3, Fig. 12.24).

book_ref.quote: The middle part of the muscle is known as the belly

blocks.prompt: 118 In an antagonistic pair, the muscle that bends the bone at a joint when it contracts is the:
blocks.explanation: The flexor bends the bone at the joint; the opposing extensor straightens it (12.3).

book_ref.quote: when one muscle, called flexor, contracts it bends the bone at joint

blocks.prompt: 119 The hamstrings that bend the lower leg at the knee are:

options.text: a group of four muscles at the front of the thigh
a group of three muscles at the back of the thigh
a single muscle of the calf

blocks.explanation: Flexion of the lower leg is by the hamstrings, three muscles at the back of the thigh; quadriceps (four, front) extend it (12.3).

book_ref.quote: It is a group of three muscles at the back of the thigh.

blocks.prompt: 120 The quadriceps originate at the ilium and femur and are inserted at the:
blocks.explanation: The quadriceps (four muscles at the front of the thigh) insert at the patella and tibia and straighten the lower leg (12.3).

book_ref.quote: with insertions at the patella (kneecap) and tibia

blocks.prompt: 121 Metabolic wastes produced by working muscles that contribute to muscle fatigue include:

options.text: lactate, hydrogen ions and reactive oxygen

blocks.explanation: Working muscles produce lactate, hydrogen ions and reactive oxygen, which contribute to fatigue (12.3).

book_ref.quote: lactate, hydrogen ions, and reactive oxygen

blocks.prompt: 122 Muscle fatigue typically improves with:
blocks.explanation: Muscle fatigue typically improves with rest; severe fatigue needs medical attention (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Muscle fatigue typically improves with rest.

blocks.prompt: 123 Muscle cramps most commonly occur in the:
blocks.explanation: Muscle cramps are sudden painful contractions lasting seconds to minutes, most commonly in the legs and feet (12.3).

book_ref.quote: most commonly occur in the legs and feet

blocks.prompt: 124 Which medication is named as a possible cause of muscle cramps?
blocks.explanation: Causes of cramps include dehydration, salt imbalance, overuse or injury, certain medications like diuretics, and diseases such as diabetes (12.3).

book_ref.quote: certain medications (like diuretics)

blocks.prompt: 125 The most common cause of tetany is:

options.text: hypocalcaemia (low level of calcium in blood)

blocks.explanation: Tetany is most commonly due to hypocalcaemia, which may result from vitamin D deficiency, renal failure or thyroid disorders (12.3).

book_ref.quote: The most common cause of tetany is hypocalcaemia

blocks.prompt: 126 Besides low calcium, tetany may also be due to a low blood level of:
blocks.explanation: Tetany may also result from other salt imbalances such as low magnesium; treatment may use calcium or magnesium supplements (12.3).

book_ref.quote: such as low level of magnesium in blood

blocks.prompt: 127 Tetanus is a severe bacterial infection caused by:
blocks.explanation: Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani, whose toxin affects the nervous system causing stiffness and spasms (12.3).

book_ref.quote: caused by Clostridium tetani

blocks.prompt: 128 Tetanus mainly affects the muscles of the:
blocks.explanation: Tetanus mainly affects the jaw and neck muscles, whereas tetany can affect hands, feet, face or larynx (12.3).

book_ref.quote: Tetanus mainly affects the jaw and neck muscles.

blocks.prompt: 129 A muscle cannot push. After it contracts, it is lengthened again by:

options.text: the pull of the opposing (antagonistic) muscle

blocks.explanation: Muscle fibres can only actively shorten (pull); the opposing antagonistic muscle's pull lengthens the relaxed muscle again (12.3, book correction).

book_ref.quote: it is lengthened again by the pull of the opposing (antagonistic) muscle

blocks.prompt: 130 When the skeleton works as a system of rods and levers, the joints serve as:
blocks.explanation: Bones are the rods, joints are the fulcrums, muscles give the effort and the weight moved is the load (12.3).

book_ref.quote: joints serve as fulcrums (pivot points) for the levers

blocks.prompt: 131 When a weight is lifted by bending the elbow, the lever is:
blocks.explanation: Book correction: the forearm bones are the lever; the elbow is the fulcrum, the biceps gives the effort and the weight is the load (12.3).

book_ref.quote: the forearm bones (radius and ulna) act as the lever
